decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: Blastoise-Mega. Lead Blastoise + Sneasler to apply immediate offensive pressure with Fake Out and powerful water/fighting attacks, threatening Talonflame, Mamoswine, and Floette. Back Whimsicott and Rotom to control speed with Tailwind and outspeed or pivot against Milotic, Musharna, and Scrafty.
decisions.notebook: Blastoise-Mega Aura Sphere handles Milotic/Scrafty/Mamoswine well. Avoid triggering Milotic Competitive. Whimsicott Tailwind manages fast Talonflame/Mamoswine threats.

decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: Floette-Eternal. Talonflame and Floette lead to establish Tailwind or immediately remove Whimsicott, limiting Prankster disruption and Sneasler’s speed advantage. Milotic is preserved for the Mega Blastoise endgame, while Mamoswine pressures Hippowdon, Rotom, and sand-based positioning. This mode avoids relying on a second Mega plan.
decisions.notebook: Opponent favors a sand-based structure with Smooth Rock Hippowdon supporting Mega Blastoise, Prankster Whimsicott speed control/disruption, and Focus Sash Unburden Sneasler with Fake Out. Mega Blastoise repeatedly uses Aura Sphere and Protect while wearing down bulky targets. Prioritize removing Whimsicott and Hippowdon, preserve Milotic for Mega Blastoise endgames, and favor Rotom pressure over Mega Floette into this matchup.

decisions.rationale: Sneasler outspeeds Talonflame (189 vs 160-195) and can use Fake Out to disrupt Talonflame's Tailwind or attack. Blastoise Mega Evolves and OHKOs Talonflame with Hydro Pump (2x effectiveness against Fire/Flying), neutralizing their speed control instantly.

Talonflame must protect because Sneasler moves first with Fake Out. Floette should Mega Evolve and pressure Blastoise with super-effective Energy Ball while avoiding an immediate exposed turn. This preserves Talonflame to establish Tailwind or threaten Sneasler next turn.
decisions.notebook: Opponent favors sand support around Mega Blastoise, with Prankster Whimsicott disruption and Focus Sash Unburden Sneasler. Mega Blastoise commonly uses Aura Sphere and Protect to wear down bulky targets. Prioritize removing Whimsicott and Hippowdon, preserve Milotic for Mega Blastoise endgames, and favor Rotom pressure over Mega Floette when feasible.

decisions.rationale: Blastoise is at 13% and threatened by priority/speed, so Protect keeps it safe while Sneasler hits Floette-Mega with super-effective Dire Claw.

Talonflame moves first and Brave Bird guarantees Sneasler's KO unless it Protects. Moonblast independently guarantees Blastoise's KO from 12%, forcing at least one foe to spend its turn protecting; if only one protects, the other is removed. This also avoids giving either threat a free attack.

Sneasler outspeeds Talonflame with Unburden and can finish it off with Dire Claw (or target Floette), while Blastoise threatens Hydro Pump onto Talonflame or Floette-Mega. Protect failed last turn for Blastoise so attacking is better than repeating Protect.

Milotic preserves the Mega Blastoise endgame while Floette’s Protect blocks Sneasler’s guaranteed Dire Claw KO. Talonflame is expendable at 1%; next turn Floette can remove Sneasler, while Milotic pressures Blastoise. Brave Bird lines risk losing Floette or failing into Protect.
decisions.notebook: Opponent favors sand support around Mega Blastoise, Prankster Whimsicott disruption, and Focus Sash Unburden Sneasler. Prioritize removing Whimsicott and Hippowdon, preserve Milotic for Mega Blastoise endgames, and favor Rotom pressure over Mega Floette when feasible. Sneasler’s Unburden is active after its Focus Sash was consumed.

decisions.rationale: Floette-Mega is active at full HP while Milotic is asleep at 35%. Sneasler has Unburden active (Speed 378) and can land a super-effective Dire Claw on Floette-Mega or close combat it, while Blastoise targets Floette-Mega with Hydro Pump to pressure the Fairy type before it can support or KO our low-HP Pokémon.

Protect preserves sleeping Milotic from both attacks and buys its recovery opportunity. Moonblast removes the active Unburden Sneasler, the immediate threat to Floette, while leaving Floette able to pressure Blastoise next turn. Targeting Blastoise allows Sneasler to attack freely.

decisions.rationale: Mamoswine preserves a healthy board piece and threatens an immediate priority Ice Shard KO on 1% Sneasler next turn, while Talonflame is already at 1% and offers little immediate value. Keeping Milotic in preserves it for the Mega Blastoise endgame despite sleep.
Blastoise-Mega and Sneasler outspeed and heavily pressure Mamoswine with Aura Sphere and Close Combat to KO it before it moves, while Milotic is still asleep.
decisions.notebook: Blastoise-Mega Aura Sphere handles Mamoswine/Scrafty cleanly. Avoid triggering Milotic Competitive.

decisions.rationale: Milotic is asleep at 47% HP with Leftovers. Blastoise-Mega has 13% HP and needs to be supported by a backline Pokémon. Bringing in Rotom gives us an Electric-type attacker to pressure Milotic while Blastoise stays in or handles whatever remains.
decisions.notebook: Milotic has Competitive and Leftovers. Talonflame has Focus Sash and Gale Wings. Avoid triggering Milotic's Competitive.

decisions.rationale: Milotic cannot act while asleep, so Protect preserves it from Blastoise. Mamoswine's priority Ice Shard guarantees the 1% Sneasler KO before Unburdened Close Combat. Removing Sneasler is safer than using a normal-priority attack into Blastoise.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Rotom outspeeds Talonflame with Choice Scarf and OHKOs its 1% HP with Thunderbolt. Blastoise uses Hydro Pump into Talonflame to guarantee its removal through potential Protect or focus sash breaks, or into Milotic if Talonflame protects. This cleanly closes out game 2.

Protect preserves Milotic from Rotom’s guaranteed Thunderbolt KO, while Brave Bird guarantees Blastoise’s KO from 12%. Taunt gives up the immediate knockout and lets Blastoise remain a threat if Talonflame is removed.

decisions.rationale: Milotic used Protect last turn, so its Protect success rate is reduced. Rotom's Thunderbolt is super-effective against Milotic (2x), and Blastoise's Hydro Pump pressures it despite the 0.5x resistance. Double targeting Milotic breaks through remaining HP.

Muddy Water acts after Rotom but guarantees the KO on Mega Blastoise from 12%, removing the immediate endgame threat. Protect is weakened and leaves Blastoise alive; Icy Wind cannot secure the KO. Talonflame has no action.

Rotom's Choice-locked Thunderbolt easily KOs Milotic (at 13% HP) with super-effective damage. Blastoise can also attack Milotic with Hydro Pump or use another move, but finishing Milotic cleanly secures the game.

Protect is the only reliable way to deny Rotom’s super-effective Thunderbolt while preserving Milotic for the Mega Blastoise endgame. Talonflame is fainted and must pass. Muddy Water’s 85% accuracy does not justify exposing Milotic to an immediate KO.
Rotom is Choice-locked into Thunderbolt, outspeeds Milotic, and hits it super-effectively for the KO. Blastoise can use Hydro Pump on Milotic just in case, or we can pressure with both.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Protect is the only line that can preserve Milotic through Rotom’s guaranteed super-effective Thunderbolt. Muddy Water would KO 1% Blastoise but leaves Milotic exposed and loses the game; Icy Wind and Recover likewise fail to stop Rotom. Talonflame has no action.

Milotic used Protect on turns 6, 8, and 9 (plus 7 after a miss), so its Protect success rate is heavily penalized (streak 2). Rotom's Thunderbolt is super-effective, and Blastoise's Hydro Pump secures the remaining 25% HP despite being not very effective. Both KO Milotic cleanly.
decisions.notebook: Milotic has Competitive, Leftovers, Muddy Water, Icy Wind, Recover, Protect.

Milotic survives Rotom's faster Thunderbolt based on the prior exchange, making the 85% KO attempt preferable to Icy Wind's weaker pressure. Protect is unreliable after consecutive uses and leaves Blastoise alive.

decisions.rationale: Milotic is at 13% HP and weak to Electric. Rotom is Choice-locked into Thunderbolt, and Whimsicott outspeeds Milotic to fire off Moonblast for chip/KOs before Milotic can use Protect or Recover effectively.
decisions.notebook: Milotic has Leftovers, Competitive, Muddy Water, Icy Wind, Recover, and Protect.

decisions.rationale: Protect is the only reliable way to avoid the immediate super-effective Thunderbolt while preserving Milotic for a possible endgame. Icy Wind cannot safely remove Whimsicott immediately, and Recover risks Prankster Encore followed by the locked Thunderbolt. Talonflame has no available action.

Milotic is at 19% HP and used Protect on turn 11. Rotom's Thunderbolt and Whimsicott's Moonblast can easily KO Milotic through its remaining HP. Attacking directly avoids any risk of Milotic using Recover or switching, securing the game.

Icy Wind is the only proactive line and can remove the weakened, Choice-locked Rotom while pressuring Whimsicott, but Milotic likely falls before acting. Protect has reduced success after last turn and risks Encore plus Thunderbolt; Recover does not address the immediate double-target threat.
decisions.notebook: Opponent consistently uses Prankster Whimsicott disruption and preserves pressure with Choice Scarf Rotom; Rotom is currently locked into Thunderbolt. Prioritize removing Whimsicott and Hippowdon, preserve Milotic for Mega Blastoise endgames, and favor Rotom pressure over Mega Floette when feasible. Sneasler's Unburden activates after its Focus Sash is consumed.

reflections.summary: Won a long late-game end-game scenario by overwhelming the remaining Milotic with Whimsicott and Choice Scarf Rotom after Blastoise and Sneasler traded effectively.
reflections.adjustment: Improve accuracy management and positioning against a late-game defensive Milotic utilizing repeated Protects and Leftovers healing.
reflections.notebook: Opponent team includes Talonflame (Focus Sash, Brave Bird, Tailwind, Taunt, Protect), Milotic (Leftovers, Competitive, Muddy Water, Icy Wind, Recover, Protect), Mamoswine (Life Orb, High Horsepower, Icicle Crash, Ice Shard, Protect), Floette-Mega (Floettite, Moonblast, Energy Ball, Protect, Helping Hand), Scrafty, and Musharna.

reflections.summary: Lost primarily because the preview plan was mismatched: Mega Floette and a passive Milotic core did not apply enough immediate pressure to Mega Blastoise, Whimsicott, and Scarf Rotom, leaving Milotic repeatedly exposed to Thunderbolt. The game was lost structurally rather than through a recorded decision error.
reflections.adjustment: Change the four and intended Mega at preview instead of defaulting to Floette-Mega/Milotic. Against this composition, prioritize immediate pressure on Whimsicott and Rotom and an Electric immunity or strong Ground attack; if no better Mega is available, bring Hippowdon or Mamoswine support and avoid making Milotic the sole answer to Mega Blastoise.
reflections.notebook: Opponent reliably combines Prankster Whimsicott disruption with Scarf Rotom pressure and can repeatedly target Milotic with Thunderbolt; Rotom may remain Choice-locked into Thunderbolt. Sneasler's Focus Sash enables Unburden and makes early damage control important. Mega Blastoise provides strong special spread pressure with Hydro Pump and carries Ice Beam/Aura Sphere. Against this core, do not default to Mega Floette plus Milotic: select a more immediately offensive Mega or Ground-based plan, remove Whimsicott early, and preserve Milotic only when it is not the team's sole defensive pivot.
